identity.title: SANA-Video: Efficient Video Generation with Block Linear Diffusion Transformer

problem.claim: Efficiently generating high-resolution, high-quality, text-aligned videos with minute-long duration on practical hardware.

contributions.claim: Introduces SANA-Video, a small diffusion model using Linear DiT with linear attention for more efficient video-token processing.
Introduces a constant-memory KV cache for block-wise autoregressive generation, providing global context at fixed memory cost for long videos.
Reports data-filtering and training strategies plus RTX 5090 deployment, targeting lower-cost and faster video generation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish SANA-Video through the combination of Linear DiT and a constant-memory KV cache for block linear attention.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report 12 days of training on 64 H100 GPUs, described as 1% of MovieGen's cost.
The authors report competitive performance against Wan 2.1-1.3B and SkyReel-V2-1.3B, with 16× faster measured latency.
The authors report reducing RTX 5090 NVFP4 inference time for a 5-second 720p video from 71 seconds to 29 seconds, a stated 2.4× speedup.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames SANA-Video as a small diffusion model for up to 720×1280 resolution and minute-long videos.
It uses linear attention in Linear DiT to reduce the cost of processing video tokens.
A block-wise autoregressive design uses a constant-memory state as a KV cache, retaining global context at fixed memory cost.
The authors report reduced training cost, competitive small-model performance, faster measured latency, and an RTX 5090 NVFP4 speedup.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs architectural mechanisms with concrete resource and latency figures, including training budget, comparison latency, and a specified hardware/precision setup.

lessons.interpretation: This makes efficiency claims more interpretable by linking them to mechanisms and explicit operating conditions.
lessons.application: For a systems paper, map each efficiency claim to its mechanism and report hardware, precision, workload, and baseline conditions alongside the number.
lessons.exception: This format is insufficient when the central claim depends primarily on quality, alignment, or safety evaluations that require their own metrics and protocols.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quality, text-video alignment, or evaluation metrics and protocols.
The comparison conditions behind the 16× latency claim and the MovieGen cost estimate are unspecified.
The abstract does not state whether the promised code and model release has occurred.
